Ibn Juzayy's commentary on surah 10, verse 1:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ We have discussed the disjointed letters (huruf al-hija') that open some surahs at the beginning of al-Baqara. ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾: a reference to the verses contained in this surah, and "the Book" here means the Qur'an. ﴿The Wise﴾: from hikma (wisdom), or from hukm (judgment), or from ahkam (rulings) in the sense that it is ordained, i.e., God has made it firm (ahkamahu Allah).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 2:

﴿Was it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them, [saying]: "Warn the people"?﴾ The hamza is for denial (al-inkar, rejection). ʿAjaban is the predicate of kana (was), and anna awhayna is its subject. Anna andhir is an explanation of the revelation (al-wahy). By "the people" here is meant the disbelievers of Quraysh and others. By "a man" here is meant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The meaning of the verse is a refutation of those who deemed prophethood unlikely or wondered that God should send a man.

﴿A sure standing (qadam sidq)﴾ means a good deed which they had sent forward. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the happiness that was decreed for them beforehand in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz). ﴿The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer."﴾ They mean what he brought of the Qur'an. It is also recited as "lasahirun" (a sorcerer), by which they mean the Prophet (ﷺ). It is possible that this statement of theirs is an explanation of their earlier wonder at prophethood, and that it is a new, independent statement.

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on Surah 10, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah﴾: an introduction to Allah and His attributes, so that they worship Him and do not associate partners with Him. It also contains a refutation of those who deny prophethood, as if He were saying: "I only call you to worship your Lord, who created the heavens and the earth, so how do you deny that, when He is the clear truth?" ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾: that is, no one intercedes with Him except after He Himself grants him permission to intercede. In this there is a refutation of the polytheists who claim that the idols intercede for them.

﴿وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقّاً﴾ *Wa'da* (ﷲ's promise) is in the accusative as a *maṣdar* (verbal noun, an infinitive-like form) that confirms the return to God mentioned earlier. *Ḥaqqan* is also in the accusative as a *maṣdar* that confirms God's promise. ﴿إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ That is, He originates the creation in this world and restores it after death in the Hereafter, and the origination is evidence for the return. ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ *Li-yajziya* gives the reason (*taʿlīl*) for the return, which is the resurrection (*al-baʿtha*). ﴿بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾ That is, with His justice in their recompense, or with their due (*qist*) for their righteous deeds.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 5–6:

﴿He is the One who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light﴾. This describes the acts of God, His power and His wisdom. Ḍiyā' (radiance) is greater than nūr (light).

﴿And He determined for it stations﴾. The pronoun refers to the moon, and the meaning is that He determined its course through stations.

﴿And the reckoning﴾. That is, the reckoning of times: of months, days and nights.

﴿God did not create that except in truth﴾ [al-Rum: 8]. That is, He did not create it in vain. The reference of "that" is to the creatures mentioned previously.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ It was said: the meaning of "yarjuna" (expect, hope) here is "yakhafuna" (fear). It was also said: "la yarjuna" means they do not hope for a good meeting with Us, so "raja'" (hope) keeps its original sense. And it may be said: "la yarjuna" means they do not anticipate it at all, and it does not occur to their minds ﴿and are content with the worldly life﴾, that is, they are satisfied that it be their portion and share ﴿and are at rest in it﴾, that is, their souls are settled and do not think of moving away from it ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ may be the first group, in which case it is coordinated as a conjunction of attributes, or they may be a different group.

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 9:

﴿Their Lord guides them by their faith﴾ That is, He makes them firm (yusaddiduhum) through their faith to uprightness, or He guides them in the Hereafter to the path of Paradise; and the latter is more preferable (arjah) given what follows it. ﴿Their call therein﴾ That is, their supplication (du'a').

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 11–12:

﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil [consequence] as eagerly as they seek to hasten the good, their term would surely have been decreed for them.﴾ That is: if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they love the hastening of good, they would have perished swiftly. It is said that the verse was revealed concerning some people regarding a person's supplication against himself, his wealth and his children. It was also said that it was revealed concerning those who said: ﴿If this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us﴾ — a rebuke, containing within it a prohibition for one who calls upon Allah in times of harm but forgets Him in times of well-being. ﴿On his side﴾ — that is, lying down. It is narrated that it was revealed concerning Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughirah because of an illness he had.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 13–17:

﴿And We certainly destroyed the generations before you﴾: an announcement that carries within it a warning to the disbelievers.

﴿That We may see how you act﴾: its meaning is that it may become manifest in existence, so that the proof is established against you by it.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾: meaning to the Quraysh.

﴿Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you"﴾: that is, I would not have recited it except by the will of Allah, for it is from Him and not from me.

﴿Nor would He have made it known to you﴾: that is, nor would I have informed you of it.

﴿Indeed I dwelt among you a lifetime before it﴾: that is, I remained among you forty years before the prophethood, and I did not speak of this until it came to me from Allah.

﴿So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses?﴾: this is a disavowal of fabricating against Allah and a demonstration of his innocence (ﷺ) of what they attributed to him of lying, and an allusion to their lying against Allah in ascribing partners to Him. ﴿Or denies His verses﴾: an explanation of their injustice in denying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 18:

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them﴾. The pronoun in "yaʿbudūn" (they worship) refers to the pagan Arabs, and "that which can neither harm them nor benefit them" refers to the idols.

﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ They used to claim that the idols would intercede for them.

﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know?"﴾ This is a refutation of their claim concerning the intercession of the idols. The meaning is: the intercession of the idols is not something known to Allah, who knows what is in the heavens and on the earth. Whatever is not known is pure non-existence, not a thing. Therefore His saying "Do you inform Allah" is an affirmation addressed to them in the form of rebuke and mockery, meaning: how can you inform Allah of what He does not know?

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 19:

﴿Mankind was not but one community﴾. This has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah [2:213] in His words: "Mankind was one community." ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded﴾, meaning the decree.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 20:

﴿And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down upon him?"﴾ They were asking for a sign from among the signs they had proposed. Yet great signs had already been sent down to him, but they did not take them into account, due to their obstinacy and their extreme misguidance. ﴿So say, "The unseen belongs only to Allah."﴾ If He wills, He acts; if He wills, He does not act. No one can know of that. ﴿So wait,﴾ that is, wait for the coming of what you have proposed. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait.﴾ That is, I am waiting for your punishment for your disbelief.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 21:

﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them﴾ This verse concerns the disbelievers, and it contains a prohibition for whoever among others is like them. Makr (scheming, deceit) here means slandering God's signs and abandoning gratitude to Him. The makr of God, which is described as swift, is His punishment of them. He called it makr by way of mushakalah (correspondence in wording) with their act, and by naming the punishment after the sin.

﴿And they sail with them﴾: The feminine pronoun in *jarayna* refers to the ships (*al-fulk*), and the pronoun in *bihim* refers to the people. In this there is a shift from address (*al-khitab*) to third person (*al-ghayba*), which is called *al-iltifat* (a shift in grammatical person). The response to *idha kuntum* is *jaatha rihun 'asifun* ("a violent wind came upon them"), and also *da'awu Allah* ("they called upon Allah").

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is a substitute (*badal*) for *zannu* ("they thought"), and its meaning is: they called upon Allah alone and disbelieved in whatever is besides Him.

﴿The enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ is in the nominative (*raf'*) as the predicate of an implied subject (*mubtada' mudmar*), its estimated form being: "That is the enjoyment." Or it may be the predicate of *innama baghyukum* ("your rebellion is only..."). The place of pause (*al-waqf*) differs according to the grammatical analysis (*i'rab*).

﴿Indeed, the likeness of the worldly life is like water which We sent down from the sky﴾: The meaning of the verse is to belittle the worldly life and to show how swiftly it passes away. It is likened to rain by which vegetation grows, and then a blight strikes that vegetation at the height of its beauty and perfection.

﴿Of that which men eat﴾: such as grain and fruits. ﴿And cattle﴾: meaning the pasture that they graze on, the grass and other things.

﴿Until the earth took on its adornment﴾: It is compared to a bride when she adorns herself with jewelry and garments.

﴿Confident that they had power over it﴾: meaning they were able to benefit from it.

﴿Then Our command came upon it﴾: meaning some calamity, such as a wind, a frost, and other things.

﴿So We made it into stubble﴾: meaning We made its crop like what has been harvested, although it had not been harvested.

﴿As if it had not flourished﴾: as if it had not been prosperous. [i.e., it had not existed. See al-Tabari.]

﴿And God invites to the Abode of Peace﴾: i.e., to Paradise. It was called the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam), meaning the abode of safety from hardship and fatigue. It has also been said that "al-Salam" here is a name of God, so the meaning is that He invites to His abode. ﴿And guides whom He wills﴾: the invitation to Paradise is mentioned in general and unrestricted terms, while guidance is specific to whomever He wills. ﴿For those who do good is the best (husna) and an increase﴾: "the best" (al-husna) is Paradise, and "the increase" is looking upon the Face of God. It has also been said that "the best" is the reward of a good deed being multiplied tenfold, and "the increase" is the multiplication beyond that up to seven hundred. The first view is more sound, due to its being reported in the hadith and to the large number of scholars who hold it. ﴿Dust (qatar)﴾: i.e., dust other than on the face.

﴿And those who earned evil deeds﴾ is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence) with an elided mudaf (annexed noun). Its implied sense is: "the recompense of those who earned evil deeds is a recompense of an evil like it," or the estimate is: "for them is a recompense of an evil like it." Alternatively, it is ma'tuf (conjoined) to "those who did good," and "recompense of an evil" is the mubtada' whose khabar (predicate) is "like it" (بمثلها).

﴿They will have no protector from God﴾: no one will shield them from the punishment of God.

﴿As though they had been covered with pieces of the night, dark﴾. Whoever reads قِطَعاً with a fatḥah on the ṭā' (the plural of قِطْعَة, "piece"), then the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of مُظْلِماً in this recitation is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) of اللَّيْل. Whoever reads قِطْعاً with a sukūn on the ṭā', then مُظْلِماً is a ṣifah (adjective) of it, or a ḥāl of اللَّيْل.

﴿Stay in your place﴾: the estimate is "keep to your place," meaning do not move until you see what God does with you.

﴿Then We separated them﴾: that is, We parted them.

﴿There every soul will experience what it sent ahead﴾: that is, it will be tested by the deeds it sent forward. It is also read تتلو with two tā's, meaning either "follows" (تتبع) or "recites it" (تقرأه) in the mushafs.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 34–35:

﴿Say, "Is there any of your associates who originates creation and then repeats it?"﴾ [The verse is] an argument against the disbelievers. If it is asked: how can they be argued with on the basis of the repetition of creation, when they do not acknowledge it? The answer is that they do acknowledge that their associates are unable to originate creation or to repeat it, and in this there is a refutation of their lordship (ribwubiyyah). Also, repetition (al-i'adah) has been placed in the position of what is agreed upon, because its proof is evident.

﴿Is there any who guides to the truth, or is it one who is not guided unless he is guided?﴾ Read as ﴿yahiddi﴾ with a doubled dal (يَهِدِّيۤ), its meaning is: he is not guided in himself, so how could he guide others. It is also read with the dal unshaddated, meaning "he guides others," but the first reading (with the doubled dal) is more forceful in argument.

﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ The ﴿مَا﴾ (ma) here is interrogative (istifhamiyyah), its meaning being confirmation (taqrir) and reproach (tawbikh); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ (lakum) is its predicate (khabar), and one pauses upon it. ﴿كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ﴾ (kayfa tahkumun), meaning: you judge falsely in your worship of other than God.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 41–42:

﴿For me is my work and for you is your work﴾ — the verse: a truce (muwada'ah), abrogated by fighting (naskh, abrogation: the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one). ﴿Among them are those who listen to you﴾ — i.e., who listen to the Qur'an. The pronoun is put in the plural by treating the word "man" (whoever) in its meaning. ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾ — the meaning is: do you want to make the deaf hear? That does not happen, especially when lack of understanding is added to deafness. ﴿Can you guide the blind?﴾ — the meaning is: do you want to guide the blind? That does not happen, especially when the blindness of insight is added to the lack of sight. Deafness and blindness here are an expression for their lack of understanding.

**Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 10, verses 48–51:**

﴿And they say, "When is this promise?"﴾ This is a statement expressing disbelief and mockery. ﴿By night﴾: that is, at night. ﴿What is it that the guilty seek to hasten?﴾ The meaning is: what is it that they seek to hasten of the punishment, which is something you have no power to bear? The phrase "what" (*mādhā*) is the answer to the conditional "if it comes upon you" (*in atākum*), and the clause is connected to *ara'aytum* (tell me). ﴿Is it then that when it befalls you, you will believe in it?﴾ The interrogative hamza of *taqrir* (affirmation through questioning) has entered upon the conjunctive *thumma* (then, "and afterwards"). The meaning is: when the punishment befalls you and you witness it, will you believe in it now? That will not benefit you, because you used to seek to hasten it and used to deny it.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 59–60:

﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision?﴾ The verse is addressed to the disbelievers of the Arabs who prohibited the baḥīrah (a she-camel whose ears were slit and released) and the sā'ibah (a camel released to graze freely), and other such things.

﴿Say: Has God permitted you [to do this], or are you inventing [lies] against God?﴾ The phrase "God has permitted you" is governed by the verb "have you considered" (ara'aytum). Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 61:

﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾. Sha'n (affair) means the matter. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is he and all of creation. For this reason, at the end of the verse, He said: ﴿and you do not do any deed﴾, addressing the group. The meaning of the verse is the comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of everything. ﴿And you do not recite from it any Qur'an﴾. The pronoun refers to the Qur'an, even though it has not been mentioned before, because what follows indicates it, as if He said: "You do not recite any portion of the Qur'an." It was said that it refers to the affair (sha'n), but the first view is more preferred, because placing the pronoun before its referent is a way of magnifying the thing. ﴿When you are deeply engaged in it﴾. It is said: afada al-rajul fi al-amr (the man plunged into the matter) when he undertook it with earnestness. ﴿And there is not hidden﴾: what is absent. ﴿From an atom's weight﴾: its weight; and dharrah (atom) refers to tiny ants. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why did he place the earth before the heavens, unlike in Surat Saba'? The answer: the heavens were placed first in Saba' because they deserve precedence, while the earth is placed first here because the mention concerns witnessing over the people of the earth. ﴿Nor smaller than that, nor greater﴾. Whoever reads them with a fatha, it is coordinated with the wording of mithqal (ma'tuf 'ala lafz mithqal). Whoever reads them with a damma, it is coordinated with its position (ma'tuf 'ala mahallih), or it is a nominative beginning (raf' bi al-ibtida').

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 62–64:

﴿And do not let their speech grieve you﴾: that is, what the disbelievers say of denial. ﴿Indeed, all might belongs to Allah﴾: a statement which contains, within it, a promise to the Prophet (ﷺ) of victory, and consolation for him. ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah as partners do not follow [in reality] except assumption﴾: regarding this there are two possibilities. (Commentary of Ibn Juzayy, al-Tashil, on Surah 10, verses 70–73)

﴿A provision in this world﴾ Its implied meaning: for them is a provision in this world.

﴿Noah﴾ It is related that his name was Abd al-Ghaffar, and he was called Noah (Nuh) only because of his frequent wailing (nawh) over himself out of fear of God.

﴿It was grievous to you﴾ That is, it was difficult and burdensome.

﴿My standing﴾ That is, my standing up to admonish you and speak with you. It has also been said that its meaning is "my place," meaning himself, like your saying: "I did that because of the place of so-and-so."

﴿So resolve upon your affair﴾ With the hamza cut (ajmi'u), from ajma'a al-amr, meaning to resolve upon a matter. It was also read with an initial alif of connection (wasl), from al-jam' (gathering).

﴿And your associates﴾ That is, what you worship besides God. Its grammatical analysis (i'rab): it is an object of accompaniment (maf'ul ma'ahu), or an object of a hidden verb, its implied meaning being: "Call upon your associates." This is according to the reading with the hamza cut. As for the reading with the connecting alif, it is coordinated (ma'tuf).

﴿Then let not your affair be hidden from you⁠—﴾ That is, let not your intention to destroy me be concealed, but let it be open, so that you openly declare it to me. It derives from your saying: "ghumma al-hilal" when the crescent did not appear. The meaning of "your affair" in both places is your destruction of Noah, peace be upon him. That is: do not fall short in destroying me, if you are able to do so.

﴿Then carry out your decision against me﴾ That is, execute whatever you intend.

The meaning of the verse is that Noah, peace be upon him, said to his people: If my calling you to God is burdensome for you, then do to me the utmost that you wish, for I do not care about you, because of my reliance upon God and my trust in Him, glory be to Him.

﴿And We made them successors﴾ That is, they succeed those who were destroyed by drowning.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 83:

﴿So none believed in Musa except a few youths from among his people⁠—﴾ The pronoun refers to Musa. The term dhurriyyah (offspring, a few youths) here means young men and lads from the Children of Israel who believed in him while fearing Fir'awn. It is also said that the pronoun refers to Fir'awn, so that dhurriyyah in this view means some of the people of Fir'awn. It is reported in this regard that they were the wife of Fir'awn, his treasurer, and the wife of his treasurer. This is far-fetched, because these people are not called dhurriyyah, and because the pronoun should refer to the nearest preceding noun. ﴿out of fear of Fir'awn and their own chiefs⁠—﴾ The pronoun refers to dhurriyyah, meaning the offspring of the Children of Israel believed, out of fear of Fir'awn and the chiefs of the Children of Israel, because the notables among the Children of Israel used to prevent their children from believing out of fear of Fir'awn. It is also said that the pronoun refers to Fir'awn, in the sense of the household of Fir'awn, as one says Rabi'ah and Mudar (for the tribes), or because he had companions who conspired on his behalf. ﴿lest he should persecute them⁠—﴾ a substitute (badal) for Fir'awn. ﴿for indeed Fir'awn was haughty in the land⁠—﴾ meaning arrogant and domineering.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 85–87:

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾: i.e., do not give them power over us to punish us, lest they say, "If these people were upon the truth, we would not have punished them," and thus be tried by that.

﴿That you two settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾: i.e., designate for them houses for prayer and worship. It was also said that He meant Alexandria.

﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾: i.e., mosques. It was also said: oriented toward the direction of the qiblah.

If it is asked: Why did He address Musa and Harun alone in His saying "an tabawwa'a (that you two settle)," and then address Bani Isra'il together with them in His saying "wa-aj'alu (and make)"? The answer: the act of "tabawwu'" (settling/designating) is among the matters specific to the prophets and those in authority (uli al-amr).

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾: a command to Musa, peace be upon him. It was also said: it is addressed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾: i.e., do not give them power over us to punish us, lest they say, "If these people were upon the truth, we would not have punished them," and thus be tried by that.

﴿That you two settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾: i.e., designate for them houses for prayer and worship. It was also said that He meant Alexandria.

﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾: i.e., mosques. It was also said: oriented toward the direction of the qiblah.

If it is asked: Why did He address Musa and Harun alone in His saying "an tabawwa'a (that you two settle)," and then address Bani Isra'il together with them in His saying "wa-aj'alu (and make)"? The answer: the act of "tabawwu'" (settling/designating) is among the matters specific to the prophets and those in authority (uli al-amr).

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾: a command to Musa, peace be upon him. It was also said: it is addressed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verse 88:

﴿Our Lord, [they have done this] so that they may lead astray from Your way.﴾ This is a supplication expressed in the form of a command. It is also said that the lam (lam of purpose, lam ka'i) is connected to his saying "you have given" (ātayta): ﴿Obliterate their wealth﴾, meaning destroy it, ﴿and harden their hearts﴾, meaning make them extremely hard, ﴿so that they will not believe﴾. This is a response to the supplication which is "harden" (ushdud), and it is a supplication expressed in the form of a negation.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 10, verses 89–92:

﴿He said: "Your prayer has been answered, so go straight"﴾ The address is to Musa and Harun, although the call to Allah is attributed only to Musa; Harun was saying "Amin" to his supplication. ﴿So go straight﴾, meaning: remain steadfast in what you are upon of calling to Allah. ﴿Then Fir'awn pursued them﴾, meaning he overtook them. It is said: "tabi'ahu" until "atba'ahu" (he followed him until he caught up with him). So said al-Zamakhshari.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: atba'a is in the meaning of taba'a, whereas ittaba'a with the doubled ta' is: seeking a trace, whether he catches up or does not catch up. ﴿There is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, meaning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. In the phrasing of Fir'awn there is ambiguity and obstinacy, since he did not state the name of Allah explicitly. ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before﴾, meaning: it was said to him, "Do you now believe, at the time of compulsion? That will not be accepted from you." ﴿We will save you﴾, meaning: We will remove you from what befell your people of reaching the bottom of the sea. It was also said: "We will cast you upon a najwa of the earth", that is, upon a high place. ﴿With your body﴾, meaning: with your physical body, without a soul. It was also said: "with your armor," for he had a golden armor by which he was recognized; the omitted element is in the position of a circumstantial clause, and the "ba'" is for accompaniment. ﴿So that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾, meaning: for those who are behind you, and they are the Children of Israel.

Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 10, verses 93–94:

﴿مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾ (a good dwelling-place): a good abode, namely Egypt and Syria. ﴿فَمَا ٱخْتَلَفُواْ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ﴾ (They did not differ until knowledge came to them). It has been said: it means their differing about their religion. It has also been said: their differing concerning the matter of Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿فَإِن كُنتَ فِي شَكٍّ﴾ (And if you are in doubt). It has been said: the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is someone else. It has also been said: this is like the saying of a speaker to his son, "If you are my son, then be dutiful to me," although he has no doubt that he is his son. But it is the nature of doubt that it is removed by asking the people of knowledge, so He commanded him to ask them. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ did not doubt and did not ask. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is by way of supposition and assumption, meaning: if you suppose that you are sitting in doubt, then ask. ﴿مِّمَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ﴾ (from what We have sent down to you). It has been said: it means the Qur'an, or the Sharia in its entirety, and this is more apparent. It has also been said: it means what was mentioned before, that the Children of Israel did not differ except after the truth had come to them. ﴿فَاسْأَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ (then ask those who read the Book). That is: those who read the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Suhayli said: they are 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Mukhayriq, and those rabbis who embraced Islam. This is far-fetched, because the verse is Meccan, and these people embraced Islam in Medina; so applying the verse in its general sense is more appropriate. ﴿فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾ (So do not be). An address to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is someone else.

Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 10, verses 96–98:

﴿Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieve﴾: that is, He decreed that they would not believe. ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it?﴾ Here "lawla" (لولا) is used for urging (tahdid), meaning "halla" (هلا, "why not"). In the irregular reading it is read as "halla." The meaning is: why was there not a town among the earlier towns that believed before the punishment descended, so that its faith would benefit it? Faith does not benefit after the punishment has been witnessed, as happened to Pharaoh. ﴿Except the people of Yunus﴾: this is an exception from "towns," because what is meant is their inhabitants. It is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed the punishment from them. It may also be a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), and the sentence then carries the sense of negation, as if he had said: no town believed except the people of Yunus. It is related in their story that Yunus, upon him be peace, warned them of the punishment, and when they saw that he had left from among them, they knew that the punishment was about to descend upon them. So they repented and humbled themselves before Allah the Exalted, and He lifted the punishment from them. ﴿And We let them enjoy for a while﴾: he means until their appointed terms that were written in eternity.

Ibn Juzayy's commentary (al-Tashil) on Surah 10, verses 99–100:

﴿Will you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ The hamza (alif al-istifham) here is for denial (al-inkar), meaning: Do you want to compel people to bring faith into their hearts and force them to it? That is not up to you; it is in the hand of God. It was also said: the meaning is, "Will you compel the people by fighting until they believe?" Or this was at the beginning of Islam, before the command to wage jihad, and was then abrogated (nuskhat) by the sword.

﴿Look﴾ is a command to reflect and contemplate the signs of God. ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who will not believe﴾: that is, those for whom God has decreed that they will not believe.
